source: Jung-Beeman, Bowden et al. (2004) Neural activity when people solve verbal problems with insight - Exp 1 fMRI
finding: Founding fMRI result: insight solutions on compound remote associate problems gave more signal than non-insight solutions in right anterior superior temporal gyrus (RH aSTG).
numbers: Exp 1: 18 recruited (10 men, 8 women), 5 excluded (poor signal or under 10 insight or noninsight responses), so 13 analysed. Solved 59% of problems; 56% of solutions labelled insight, 41% no insight, 2% other. Peak RH aSTG difference 0.25% over 6 s window (0.30% at one TR); 12 of 13 subjects showed 0.03% to 0.35% more signal for insight.
limits: Small N (13). Insight label is self-report. Verbal CRA problems only. Authors note low signal (72% and 83% of brainwide average) in two other foci.
agent_relevance: Self-reported insight tags a distinct mechanism (distant semantic links) but in a tiny sample; weak basis for any model-side signal.

source: Jung-Beeman, Bowden et al. (2004) Neural activity when people solve verbal problems with insight - Exp 2 EEG
finding: EEG test: a burst of gamma activity over right anterior temporal electrodes began about 0.3 s before insight solutions, not non-insight ones. A posterior alpha effect was also significant.
numbers: Exp 2: 19 new subjects (9 men, 10 women). Of correct solutions, 56% insight (SD 8.4) vs 42% non-insight (SD 9.0), t(18)=3.47, p=0.003. Response times did not differ (9.94 s vs 9.25 s, t<1). No significant theta or beta effects; a frontal 4-Hz effect could be eye-movement artifact.
quote: The FMRI and EEG results reported here conclusively demonstrate that solving verbal problems with insight requires at least one additional component
limits: N=19, one lab. Scalp EEG localisation is coarse. Effect depends on the self-reported insight contrast. Timing is about 300 ms before a button press.
agent_relevance: There is no way to read such a burst in a language model; the useful part is that insight solutions are tagged by distant semantic links.

source: Sandkuhler and Bhattacharya (2008) Deconstructing insight: EEG correlates of insightful problem solving
finding: Independent EEG study with trial-by-trial suddenness and restructuring ratings. It asked whether the right-temporal gamma burst could be confirmed. The main gamma effects appeared over parieto-occipital areas (38-44 Hz) rather than right temporal.
numbers: 21 participants (11 female, median age 26.4). 36 CRA problems, 45 s limit. Sudden solutions N=302 vs non-sudden N=88 (trials pooled): two gamma clusters at 38-44 Hz in parieto-occipital area. Correct without hint 38.8% (SD 9.6), incorrect 11.2% (SD 8.0). Median per person: 17 sudden correct vs 1 non-sudden correct.
quote: Can the EEG results from Jung-Beeman and others be confirmed, who reported gamma activity at right temporal region beginning at 300 ms
limits: Trials pooled across people; very few non-sudden trials. Different design (hints, impasse), so a partial, not direct, replication.
agent_relevance: Gamma with insight shows up again but the scalp location moves. Do not hard-code where a signal sits.

source: Sandkuhler and Bhattacharya (2008) - impasse and alpha findings
finding: Mental impasse had its own EEG signature: parieto-occipital gamma and occipital theta differed between impasse and timeout trials. A strong alpha rise over right temporal area just before hint presentation was read as inhibition or weak unconscious processing of the solution.
numbers: Median trials per person: impasse 31 (range 0-57); timeout 12 (0-55); post-hint correct after impasse 13 (0-31). Control tasks: 21 of 22 correct when true solution shown, 10 of 11 correct when false solution shown. Right parieto-occipital gamma before the hint was stronger for impasse-then-timeout than impasse-then-solved.
limits: Authors' alpha interpretation is speculative. Cluster-based stats on a small sample.
agent_relevance: Supports impasse as a separate measurable stage; it matches the stuck state in our schema but only through scalp EEG.

source: Aihara et al. (2017) Anodal tDCS of the right anterior temporal lobe did not significantly affect verbal insight
finding: Failed replication of the causal right-ATL claim: anodal right ATL tDCS did not change verbal insight (RAT), non-verbal insight or non-insight performance. Two electrode montages tested.
numbers: 66 subjects, within-subjects, active vs sham on 2 days. Bi-cephalic montage (anode right ATL, cathode left ATL) and extra-cephalic montage (cathode on left cheek). No significant effect on any task.
quote: These results failed to reinforce previous tDCS findings demonstrating a causal relationship between the right ATL
limits: Japanese kanji RAT with distracter fillers. Non-verbal insight null is called inconclusive for lack of power. Current and montage differ from Chi and Snyder.
agent_relevance: The causal story for the right temporal lobe is fragile. Another reason not to port a hemispheric rule into an agent.

source: Chi and Snyder (2011) Facilitate insight by non-invasive brain stimulation
finding: Cathodal left ATL plus anodal right ATL tDCS raised solving of matchstick insight problems about three-fold compared with sham.
numbers: 67 recruited, 60 analysed. Hardest problem (Type 2): 20% solved with sham vs 60% in L-minus R-plus group by 6 min (Fisher p=0.022). Easier Type 3: 45% sham vs 85% (p=0.019). Logrank p=0.008 for L-R+ vs sham. About 20 per group.
quote: the strongest cognitive enhancement we are aware of for a brain stimulation study
limits: Small between-subjects groups, non-verbal matchstick task. Exploratory handling of the L+R- group after baseline concerns. Authors list limits themselves.
agent_relevance: A very large effect from small groups is a replication-risk pattern; Aihara 2017 did not reproduce it with other tasks.

source: 2020 Scientific Reports: TDCS to the right anterior temporal lobe facilitates insight problem-solving
finding: Positive causal test with high-definition tDCS: rATL stimulation raised overall CRA solving and specifically insight-labelled solutions, vs pre-stimulation, sham and left frontopolar stimulation. Effect lasted at least 20 minutes after stimulation.
numbers: Three groups (rATL active, sham, left frontopolar), about 110 participants in total (F tests with 107 error df). Group x time F(4,214)=3.23, p=0.01, partial eta-squared 0.057. Between groups F(2,107)=3.64, p=0.03, partial eta-squared 0.064. Solving style x group F(2,107)=3.15, p=0.015.
limits: Small to medium effects. Insight label is self-report after brief training. Conflicts with Aihara 2017 (different task and montage). Authors not read from page text.
agent_relevance: Causal evidence is mixed (positive 2011, 2020; null 2017). Treat right temporal lobe as a hypothesis.

source: Tik et al. (2018) Ultra-high-field fMRI insights on insight: Neural correlates of the Aha!-moment
finding: 7 T fMRI with a German RAT: insight solutions engaged the LEFT anterior middle temporal gyrus plus subcortical areas: bilateral thalamus, hippocampus and dopaminergic midbrain (VTA, nucleus accumbens, caudate).
numbers: Final sample 29 subjects (15 f, 14 m, age 27.7 +/- 3.7). German RAT validated with an online sample of 163 subjects.
limits: Cortical effect is left, not right, temporal. Button press marks the Aha event, so timing is coarse.
agent_relevance: Insight carries a reward or relief component. A scaffold could mimic it with an explicit check-and-commit step, but there is no direct readout.

source: Becker et al. (2020) Verbal insight revisited: fMRI evidence for early processing in bilateral insulae
finding: Solutions later given with an AHA experience were predicted by early activity in bilateral anterior insulae shortly after trial onset; the same insulae were more active at solution time for no-AHA solutions. This challenges the view that insight arises only from late restructuring.
numbers: 30 right-handed fMRI participants (23 f, 7 m, age 18-31) plus a 26-person eye-tracking control. Timing x solution experience interaction significant in bilateral anterior insula. Early effect independent of semantic priming.
limits: Salience-network interpretation tentative. Modified CRA with priming.
agent_relevance: Early preparation matters more than a late burst, which suggests problem framing at the start is the lever.

source: 2024 Human Brain Mapping EEG study: Time course of EEG power during creative problem-solving with insight or remote thinking
finding: French modified RAT with EEG: insight solving went with alpha and gamma power increase in a LEFT temporal cluster before the response, plus frontal theta. Semantic remoteness went with alpha (left parieto-temporal), beta (right fronto-temporal), theta (bilateral frontal).
numbers: 23 recruited, 21 analysed (12 women, mean age 22.95). 100 trials per person. Gamma band 31-60 Hz.
limits: Small N. Left not right temporal for insight, a mismatch with Jung-Beeman 2004. Different language and task.
agent_relevance: Insight gamma direction is repeatable (increase) while laterality is not.

source: Dietrich and Kanso (2010) A review of EEG, ERP, and neuroimaging studies of creativity and insight
finding: Review of 72 experiments (63 articles): divergent thinking and artistic results inconsistent; insight studies more consistent and point to anterior cingulate and prefrontal areas. Creativity is not especially a right-brain, defocused-attention, low-arousal or alpha-synchronisation phenomenon.
numbers: 72 experiments in 63 articles across divergent thinking, artistic creativity and insight.
quote: creative thinking does not appear to critically depend on any single mental process or brain region
limits: Seen only as abstract text (Europe PMC and search); full paper not opened. Pre-dates the 2018-2026 work.
agent_relevance: The right-brain framing is a weak basis for design; supports leaving such a rule out of the scaffold.

source: Mihov, Denzler and Forster (2010) Hemispheric specialization and creative thinking: a meta-analytic review of lateralization of creativity
finding: Vote-counting meta-analysis: relative right-hemisphere dominance during creative thinking; no difference by verbal vs figural, holistic vs analytical, or context-dependent vs independent tasks.
numbers: Effect size given as Cramer's phi (value not read).
limits: Abstract only. Vote counting is a weak method. Conflicts with Dietrich and Kanso on how strong the right lean is.
agent_relevance: Even the pro-right-hemisphere summary is a lean, not a rule.

source: Meta-analysis (2018) Tracking the neurodynamics of insight: A meta-analysis of neuroimaging studies, Biological Psychology
finding: Two ALE meta-analyses found an integrated insight network including right medial frontal gyrus, left inferior frontal gyrus, left amygdala and right hippocampus, with regions recruited differently across four Wallas-style stages.
numbers: Two ALE meta-analyses (all studies; stage-specific). Study counts not read.
limits: Abstract only (Europe PMC). Authors not read. No right anterior temporal peak named in the abstract.
agent_relevance: The convergent region list does not centre on the Jung-Beeman site.

source: Meta-analysis (2016) Is creative insight task-specific? Coordinate-based meta-analysis of insightful problem solving, Int J Psychophysiol
finding: Three ALE meta-analyses (compound remote associates, prototype heuristic, Chinese character chunk decomposition) found largely non-overlapping regions across tasks. CRA relied on right parahippocampal, superior frontal and inferior frontal gyri.
numbers: Three task-specific ALE meta-analyses; study counts not read.
limits: Abstract only. Authors not read. Task dependence means a RAT signature may not carry to other insight tasks.
agent_relevance: Insight is heterogeneous, so one neural marker could not map onto one scaffold operator.

source: Kounios et al. (2008) The origins of insight in resting-state brain activity, Neuropsychologia
finding: Resting EEG before anagram solving differed between people who solve more by insight and those who solve more by search: signs of diffuse attention and right-lateralised hemispheric asymmetry.
numbers: Subjects split into two groups by proportion of insight vs search anagram solutions; sample size not read.
limits: Abstract only. Trait-like group difference, not a trial-level predictor.
agent_relevance: Insight tendency is a person-level style; the model analogue is a mode or prompt setting, not a readout.

source: 2025 Scientific Reports fMRI study: Neural correlates and dynamical brain states of creative insight in a spatial problem task
finding: In matchstick arithmetic, default mode network was more active for insight solutions; executive control network for quick and analytical solutions. A hidden Markov model gave distinct brain states per strategy, with high state variability during long insight solutions.
numbers: 16 participants (fMRI). GLM plus hidden Markov model.
limits: Very small N. Spatial, non-verbal task, so not comparable to RAT results. Authors not read.
agent_relevance: Insight is linked to loose, flexible network dynamics rather than to a single burst.

source: The white matter of Aha! moments (BMC Psychology 2026), DTI study
finding: Individual tendency to solve CRA by insight related to fractional anisotropy in left dorsal tracts (arcuate, posterior arcuate, SLF III), a left-lateralised substrate.
numbers: 38 participants. Left omnibus tests significant for FA after controlling age and gender; MD trended only (p=0.032, q=0.081).
limits: Small N, correlational, structural not functional.
agent_relevance: No online use; shows that insight style differs by person.

source: Illumination Onset: a theoretical neuroscience framework for the sudden Aha moment (Behavioral Sciences 2026)
finding: Theory paper. Alpha decreases and gamma increases near solutions are called dominance inversion, a drop in top-down precision. Links ACC to surprise detection, serotonin to gamma, and compares seizure onset as boundary case.
numbers: No new data. Cites studies of alpha decrease and gamma increase near reported solutions.
limits: Untested theory. It says alpha decreases, while Jung-Beeman 2004 and Sandkuhler 2008 report alpha increases over right-sided areas, so alpha direction is disputed.
agent_relevance: Lowering dominance of the established frame maps to a reframe operator, not to a measurable signal.

source: REM sleep favors the restructuring of problem-related semantic associations (Communications Biology 2026)
finding: After a 90-minute nap, REM reshaped problem-related semantic networks (more remote links, fewer strong solution-irrelevant links) compared with wake. REM alone did not raise solving success.
numbers: 90-min incubation in REM, NREM only, or wake; restructuring measured as pre-post change in semantic network properties. Participant count not read.
limits: Riddle task; restructuring without a success gain.
agent_relevance: Restructuring and solving can dissociate; a reframed state is not a correct answer.

source: Do Semantic Distance Tests Actually Predict Creativity in LLMs? Evidence for Jagged Creativity (arXiv 2605.13450, NeurIPS 2026)
finding: Large systematic study: the Remote Associates Test is effectively a proxy for general capability in LLMs, not a specific predictor of creativity. No semantic distance test predicts output diversity.
numbers: DAT vs Hivemind r=+0.30 but partial r given general ability -0.01; NoveltyBench Utility r=+0.06. Arena creative writing correlates R=0.87 with MMLU-Pro, capping specificity at 0.49. PACE rank correlation with creative writing 0.74 but 0.66 with general capability.
limits: Preprint; number of models not read.
agent_relevance: RAT scores in LLMs mostly reflect general ability, so RAT-based insight claims about models should be discounted.

source: Large Language Models are Fixated by Red Herrings: Only Connect Wall dataset (arXiv 2306.11167, 2023)
finding: Used Only Connect Walls, a RAT-like task with built-in red herrings, to test fixation (Einstellung) in LLMs. Best few-shot result (GPT-4, 10-shot) was about 41-45% F1, far below human performance.
numbers: Split 62 train, 62 validation, 494 test walls. A prediction is judged correct near ROUGE-1 or BERTScore F1 of 0.5. About 8.2% of the best model's predicted connections wrongly contained clue words.
limits: Human baseline not extracted. Synthetic OCW-Randomized and OCW-WordNet variants not read in detail.
agent_relevance: Models fixate on lure items, the stuck-frame problem that reframing operators address.

source: CREATE: Creativity Evaluation of VLMs using the Visual Remote Associates Test (arXiv 2610.18569, Oct 2026)
finding: 155 visual RAT problems. Humans solved 22.8% on average; only one of 11 VLMs beat the human average zero-shot (32.5%) and no other model solved more than 12.5%.
numbers: Human study N=25, 16 problems each from an 80-problem subset; 22.5% first half vs 23.0% second half; 70% of problems solved by at least one of 5 people. 7 open-weight and 4 proprietary VLMs.
limits: Visual cues; associative ability depends on cue concepts given in text. Not a neural study.
agent_relevance: RAT-type association remains hard for models in vision form.

source: The Illusion of Insight in Reasoning Models (arXiv 2601.00514, 2026)
finding: Tests whether R1-style Aha shifts are real insight. Mid-reasoning shifts were rare, did not become more frequent with training and seldom improved accuracy. Artificially triggering reconsideration under high entropy did help.
numbers: 1M+ reasoning traces, hundreds of GRPO checkpoints, three reasoning domains. Shifts in 6.31% of traces. Externally triggered reconsideration under high entropy: +8.41 percentage points on MATH-500, smaller gains on crosswords and Rush Hour.
quote: reasoning shifts are rare, do not become more frequent with training, and seldom improve accuracy
limits: GRPO-tuned Qwen2.5 and Llama models; may differ for larger models.
agent_relevance: Supports triggering a reframe by rule under uncertainty rather than waiting for a spontaneous Aha.

source: R1-Zero's Aha Moment in Visual Reasoning on a 2B Non-SFT Model (arXiv 2503.05132, 2025)
finding: Reports a replication of R1-style emergent self-reflection and longer responses in a 2B vision-language model trained with RL on SAT data.
numbers: 59.47% on CVBench, about 30% above the base model and about 2% above the SFT setting.
limits: Aha here means self-reflection and length growth, not a neural or insight measure; 2601.00514 questions what it means.
agent_relevance: Aha as a training artifact, not a usable signal.

source: Jung-Beeman, Bowden et al. (2004) - alpha and artifact caveats
finding: The 2004 paper itself flags weak spots: low fMRI signal in secondary foci and a possible eye-movement artifact behind a frontal 4-Hz effect. Only the right anterior temporal findings were called conclusive.
numbers: Two secondary foci had signal at 72% and 83% of brainwide average. Theta (5-8 Hz) and beta (13-20 Hz) tests: no significant effects.
limits: Self-assessment by authors.
agent_relevance: Founding result rests on 13 fMRI and 19 EEG subjects; later work (b03, b05, b10) did not reproduce the same site.
